issues.description: The template's QFT class defines the forward QFT method with the name `_qft_circuit(...)`, whereas the solution implements it as `qft_circuit(...)`. The inverse QFT in the solution calls `self.qft_circuit(...)`, but the template does not provide a `qft_circuit` method, only `_qft_circuit`. This name/signature mismatch between template and solution will confuse students (and break any tests or examples expecting `qft_circuit`) and prevents straightforward reuse of the inverse implementation shown in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the forward QFT method name consistent across template and solution. Rename the template method `_qft_circuit` to `qft_circuit` (and update any internal references), or alternatively change the solution to call `_qft_circuit`. Ensure the problem statement/tests reference the same method name (`qft_circuit`) to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The QFT 3-qubit implementation method name differs between template and solution: the template defines the forward QFT method as `_qft_circuit`, while the solution provides it as `qft_circuit`. This inconsistency can confuse students (and automated tests) about which method to implement/call for Exercise 6.1 and for implementing the inverse (which the solution calls via `self.qft_circuit(...)`).
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single, consistent method name for the forward QFT across template and solution. Either rename the template method `_qft_circuit` to `qft_circuit` (preferred) or rename the solution method to `_qft_circuit` and ensure the inverse implementation calls the same name. Update any tests or references accordingly so students have a clear, unambiguous target to implement.
